registered_before: any candidate in Steps 2-4 was evaluated on the 2025 holdout

incumbent.definition: football/engine.js v1 recursion with the Step 1 correctness fixes (defence mirrored from the opponent's offence row, QB starts absorbed by training's rule, PMF win probability), its v1 feature set and two-stage ridge (strength lambda 60, context lambda 200) refitted walk-forward
incumbent.why: Step 1 fixes are correctness fixes and ship regardless; every Step 2-4 change is judged against this, not against the bugged served model

sources: nflverse/nfldata games.csv (schedule, scores, closing consensus spread/total/moneylines, rest, roof, surface, QB ids, location)
nflverse-data stats_player_week 1999-2026 (QB game log; RB/WR/TE production for the personnel prior)
football/venues/nfl_stadiums.json (verified stadium coordinates and time zones; three historical home cities added for STL/SD/OAK)
not_used: preseason win totals: nfldata win_totals.csv ends at 2020, so a win-total prior can be neither validated on 2025 nor served for 2026 (INACTIVE)
any paid feed (PFF grades, etc.): not owned (INACTIVE)

protocol.validation_method: walk-forward: for each season S in 2010..2024 the ridge weights, the context model, the margin PMF and any calibration are fitted on seasons 2002..S-1 only and S is predicted pregame, game by game, from the rating state before each game
protocol.holdout_method: the same walk-forward step for S = 2025 (weights fitted on 2002..2024); 2025 is never used to choose a hyperparameter, a feature or a toggle
protocol.rows_scored: every 2010-2025 game (regular and postseason) with a closing spread and a final score
protocol.baseline: the closing line: closing consensus spread as the margin forecast; de-vigged closing moneylines as the win probability (moneylines are complete from 2010)

secondary: calibration: ECE over 10 equal-width bins and the logistic calibration slope
ATS vs the close at |model - close| >= 1, 2, 3
home lean: mean model home margin minus mean closing home margin

selection_rule: Within each candidate family the setting with the lowest 2010-2024 walk-forward margin MAE is selected (log loss for a probability-only change; ties broken by log loss). A family's selected setting is a FINALIST only if it also improves on the incumbent's 2010-2024 MAE and log loss.
promotion_rule: A finalist is PROMOTED only if, on the 2025 holdout, it beats the incumbent on margin MAE AND on log loss (a probability-only change: log loss AND Brier, MAE unchanged). Promoted changes accumulate step by step: each step's incumbent is the previous step's result. Anything that only helps 2026 to date, or one game, is never a reason to promote.
disclosure: Every variant evaluated is written to football/research/nfl_v2/results/variants.jsonl with its validation metrics; every holdout evaluation is written there too, flagged, so the number of looks at 2025 is on the record.

P0_wide_geometric.what: v1 structure (prior weight carry*(1-alpha)^n), widened grid

P1_hyperbolic.what: prior weight k/(k+n), n = games played this season; this season's evidence an equal-weight mean of opponent-adjusted games

P2_personnel.what: offseason continuity from nflverse snap counts and week-1 rosters: RB rushing-EPA carried in/out, WR/TE receiving-EPA carried in/out, OL share of last season's snaps returning; QB changes are the QB layer's (absorbed every game since Step 1). Each enters the strength model scaled by the club's prior weight, so it fades as the season is played; weights by ridge. Measurable from 2013.

P3_market.what: a market rating learned only from closing spreads of games already played (previous weeks, previous seasons), entered as a strength feature; its weight by ridge

H1_season_hfa.what: home field from home margins of earlier seasons, weighted rho^(age), shrunk toward the long-run mean with m pseudo-games, plus this season's games to date; both models fitted without an intercept; every home constant zero at a neutral site

H2_travel_tz.what: away-minus-home travel (1000 km), time zones crossed, and a west-coast team in a 1 pm ET kickoff, as context features

H3_venue_terms.what: the context model's dome and grass terms (the outdoor-turf home term)

T1_split_od.what: pass offence, pass defence, rush offence, rush defence (and overall offence/defence) as separate features instead of net_pass/net_rush/net_epa

T2_recency.what: this season's evidence weighted lambda^(age) inside the season

T3_garbage_time.what: team-game efficiency from play-by-play with garbage time removed

variants.G1: second half, offence win probability < 0.10 or > 0.90 dropped

T3_garbage_time.control: G0: the same play-by-play, unfiltered (isolates the filter from the source change)

T4_isotonic.what: isotonic (pool-adjacent-violators) map of the win probability, fitted on earlier seasons' out-of-sample predictions, clipped to [0.01, 0.99]

T5_net_pts_fix.what: net_pts = (pts_for - pts_against) home minus away (audit_report.md section 6.7; v1 adds points allowed)

step4.combinations: every toggle that is individually a finalist, then their combinations; each combination's holdout result disclosed

seen_before_registration: 2025 descriptive statistics during the audit: mean home margin 2.18 and mean closing home spread 1.58 (non-neutral regular season); 2010-2025 closing home favourites of 6-7.5 finished p10/p50/p90 -9/7/26

the corrected v1 (the incumbent) replayed by tools/football/validate_pricing.js over 2016-2025, 2025 included: pooled spread MAE 10.187 vs close 9.777 (football/validation/pricing_nfl.json). No candidate has been evaluated on any season.

weekly_loop.registered_before: the weekly loop's first evaluation of any candidate (its first run, 2026 week 6, found no repeat pattern and evaluated none)
weekly_loop.pattern_rule: a pattern in the served model's season-to-date replayed residuals REPEATS when |t| >= 2 on at least 30 games AND its weekly readings point the same way in at least 60% of the weeks it can be read in. Patterns: home lean (mean residual at home sites); each card component's slope (base strength, passing, rushing, quarterback, rest/travel, context); the base strength's current and prior parts' slopes; the slope on (close - model); the slope on the model margin

candidate_families.prior:current / prior:prior: P0: alpha and alpha_pts x1.4 (prior too sticky) or /1.4 (too loose); carry -/+0.05 within [0.30, 0.95]. P1 (if the served prior is hyperbolic): k and k_pts x0.67 or x1.5
candidate_families.component:base_strength / scale: ridge_strength: the strength model's ridge lambda x2 (over-weighted) or x0.5 (under-weighted)
candidate_families.component:context: H3_venue_terms: drop the dome and grass terms

weekly_loop.cap: at most 6 candidates per run, in the order above
weekly_loop.evaluation: the backtest of Steps 2-4 unchanged (backtest.js), on every season: 2010 through the season being played (full), the 2025 holdout, and 2010-2025 (without the season being played)
weekly_loop.promotion_rule: PROMOTED only if it beats the served model on margin MAE AND log loss on all three of: the full window, the 2025 holdout, 2010-2025. Among several that pass, the lowest full-window MAE. The served model is never changed by anything that only helps the season being played, or one game.
weekly_loop.versioning: a promotion bumps the minor version (edgedesk_nfl_v2.N.0), trains through the last completed season (train.js writeParams), archives the params under versions/ and records the version, every candidate's result and the event in registry.json; supabase/nfl_model_registry.sql is regenerated from it. Rollback restores an archived version (weekly_loop.js --rollback).
weekly_loop.disclosure: every weekly evaluation, the served model's included, is appended to results/variants.jsonl with holdout_looked = true: each run is a look at 2025, and the count of looks is on the record

round_2.registered_before: any round-2 candidate was evaluated on any season

incumbent.definition: the served model: v1 with the Step 1 fixes and the net_pts sign fix (T5)

round_2.why: RESULTS.md 'Known limitations': a starter with little history is shrunk to a league-average QB prior (-0.04 EPA/dropback), so an injury to an elite starter barely moves the number (2026 week 7 DAL @ PHI, Hurts out: QB row -0.21 against a ~8-point market move); and the raw-scale ridge shrinks the EPA terms once net_pts is corrected

Q1_qb_prior.what: the QB layer's prior and shrinkage (football/nfl_model.js qbEff: value x n/(n+k) + prior x k/(n+k)) — a starter with few games is pulled toward a lower prior
Q1_qb_prior.note: the incumbent pair (-0.04, 12) is not a candidate

Q2_qb_out.what: a strength-model feature qb_out_diff = home_out - away_out, where a side is OUT when its starter is not its regular starter: the QB with the most starts in the club's last 8 games (ties to the most recent). Its weight is fitted by the ridge like every other term

S1_standardize.what: the strength model's features scaled to unit standard deviation on each fit's training rows before the ridge (weights mapped back to raw scale, so serving is unchanged)

candidates.combinations: every family whose selected setting is a finalist, then their combinations; each combination's holdout result disclosed

round_2.selection_rule: as Steps 2-4: within a family the lowest 2010-2024 walk-forward MAE (ties by log loss); a FINALIST beats the incumbent on 2010-2024 MAE AND log loss
round_2.promotion_rule: as Steps 2-4: PROMOTED only if it also beats the incumbent on the 2025 holdout on MAE AND log loss; the promoted version is edgedesk_nfl_v2.1.0
seen_before_registration: the 2026 week 7 cards (DAL @ PHI) and every Steps 1-4 result in results/step1-4.json and RESULTS.md, 2025 holdout included: these candidates are motivated by those results, which is why each must still win on 2010-2024 first and the 2025 holdout second
no round-2 candidate has been evaluated on any season

round_3.registered_before: any round-3 candidate was evaluated on any season

incumbent.definition: the served model: v2.0.0 + round 2 (QB prior -0.16 / shrink 6, qb_out_diff, standardised strength ridge lambda 240)

why: the backup-QB gap is narrowed, not closed: 2026 week 7 DAL @ PHI (Hurts out) is still 5.1 points off a market that prices the absence at about 8; the round-2 out term is one average for every replacement, whoever he replaces
two round-2 picks sit on the edge of their grids (QB prior -0.16 and shrink 6; lambda 240)
Step 4 chose T5 over T2 + T5 by 2025 MAE, which the holdout rule forbids; in-season recency is an open candidate (RESULTS.md, round 2)

Q3_qb_out_gap.what: a strength-model feature qb_out_gap_diff = home gap - away gap, where a side's gap is (the regular starter's QB value - the starter's QB value) when the side is OUT (round 2's definition), else 0; QB values are qbEff under the configuration's prior and shrinkage. Its weight is fitted by the ridge like every other term; qb_out_diff stays

Q1x_qb_prior.what: the round-2 grid extended past its edge
Q1x_qb_prior.note: the incumbent pair (-0.16, 6) is not a candidate

S1x_lambda.what: the standardised strength ridge past its edge

T2r_recency.what: in-season recency lambda (Step 4 T2) on the round-2 incumbent

candidates.combinations: every family whose selected setting is a finalist, then their combinations (each family at its selected setting)

round_3.selection_rule: within a family the lowest 2010-2024 walk-forward MAE (ties by log loss)
round_3.finalist_rule: beats the incumbent on 2010-2024 MAE AND log loss, AND has the lower MAE in at least 9 of the 15 validation seasons (new this round: the 2025 holdout has gated 14 earlier decisions, so a validation edge must be broad, not one or two seasons)
round_3.promotion_rule: a finalist is PROMOTED only if it beats the incumbent on MAE AND log loss on all three windows of the weekly loop gate (weekly_loop.js gate: the full backtest 2010 to the season being played, the 2025 holdout, 2010-2025). Step 4 T2 recency on the Step 3 base: lambda 0.95 was its best (2010-2024 10.392 / 0.6342; 2025 10.220 / 0.6383) and T2 + T5 beat T5 on 2010-2024 by 0.0009 MAE
